passages.text: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations, for you have played the harlot against your God; you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.
passages.sermon:
Israel, do not rejoice.
Do not celebrate like the other nations.
You have been unfaithful to your God.
You have acted like a harlot.
You have loved the wages of sin.
You have sought payment on every threshing floor.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּשְׂמַ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל׀ אֶל־ גִּיל֙ כָּֽעַמִּ֔ים כִּ֥י זָנִ֖יתָ מֵעַ֣ל אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אָהַ֣בְתָּ אֶתְנָ֔ן עַ֖ל כָּל־ גָּרְנ֥וֹת דָּגָֽן׃

passages.text: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them.
passages.sermon:
Israel has turned away from God.
God is judging Israel.
The threshing floor will not provide food for Israel.
The winepress will not give Israel what they need.
The new wine will fail Israel.
Israel will not have enough to eat or drink.
passages.original: גֹּ֥רֶן וָיֶ֖קֶב לֹ֣א יִרְעֵ֑ם וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יְכַ֥חֶשׁ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: They will not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
passages.sermon: Israel will not stay in the land of the LORD.\r\nEphraim will go back to Egypt.\r\nIn Assyria, they will eat unclean food.
passages.original: לֹ֥א יֵשְׁב֖וּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֤ב אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבְאַשּׁ֖וּר טָמֵ֥א יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him, but will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves; it will not enter the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD.
Their sacrifices will not please the LORD.
Their sacrifices will be like the bread eaten by mourners.
Anyone who eats this bread will become defiled.
Their bread will be only for themselves.
Their bread will not enter the house of the LORD.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִסְּכ֨וּ לַיהוָ֥ה׀ יַיִן֮ וְלֹ֣א יֶֽעֶרְבוּ־ לוֹ֒ זִבְחֵיהֶ֗ם כְּלֶ֤חֶם אוֹנִים֙ לָהֶ֔ם כָּל־ אֹכְלָ֖יו יִטַמָּ֑אוּ כִּֽי־ לַחְמָ֣ם לְנַפְשָׁ֔ם לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?
passages.sermon:
Israel faces punishment from God.
God will not allow Israel to remain in His land.
Ephraim will return to Egypt.
Ephraim will eat unclean food in Assyria.
Israel cannot offer wine to the LORD.
Their sacrifices will not please God.
Their sacrifices will be like the bread of mourners.
All who eat will be defiled.
Their bread will be only for themselves.
Their bread will not enter the house of the LORD.
God asks Israel a question.
What will you do on the appointed day?
What will you do on the day of the LORD’s feast?
passages.original: מַֽה־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ לְי֣וֹם מוֹעֵ֑ד וּלְי֖וֹם חַג־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles, and thorns will overrun their tents.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel try to escape destruction.
They run from danger.
Egypt will gather them.
Memphis will bury them.
Their silver is precious to them.
Thistles will take their silver.
Thorns will fill their tents.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֤ה הָֽלְכוּ֙ מִשֹּׁ֔ד מִצְרַ֥יִם תְּקַבְּצֵ֖ם מֹ֣ף תְּקַבְּרֵ֑ם מַחְמַ֣ד לְכַסְפָּ֗ם קִמּוֹשׂ֙ יִֽירָשֵׁ֔ם ח֖וֹחַ בְּאָהֳלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived— let Israel know it. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane, because of the greatness of your iniquity and hostility.
passages.sermon:
God warned Israel through the prophet Hosea.
God said the days of punishment have come.
The days of retribution have arrived.
Israel must know this.
People now call the prophet a fool.
They call the inspired man insane.
They do this because Israel’s sin is very great.
There is much hostility among the people.
passages.original: בָּ֣אוּ׀ יְמֵ֣י הַפְּקֻדָּ֗ה בָּ֚אוּ יְמֵ֣י הַשִׁלֻּ֔ם יֵדְע֖וּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֱוִ֣יל הַנָּבִ֗יא מְשֻׁגָּע֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָר֔וּחַ עַ֚ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנְךָ֔ וְרַבָּ֖ה מַשְׂטֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman, along with my God, yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God!
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
The prophet serves as a watchman for Ephraim.
The prophet stands with my God.
A snare traps the prophet on every path.
Hostility fills the house of the prophet’s God.
passages.original: צֹפֶ֥ה אֶפְרַ֖יִם עִם־ אֱלֹהָ֑י נָבִ֞יא פַּ֤ח יָקוֹשׁ֙ עַל־ כָּל־ דְּרָכָ֔יו מַשְׂטֵמָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

passages.text: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.
passages.sermon:
The people have deeply corrupted themselves.
They have done evil like the people did in the days of Gibeah.
God will remember their guilt.
God will punish their sins.
passages.original: הֶעְמִֽיקוּ־ שִׁחֵ֖תוּ כִּימֵ֣י הַגִּבְעָ֑ה יִזְכּ֣וֹר עֲוֺנָ֔ם יִפְק֖וֹד חַטֹּאותָֽם׃ס

passages.text: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves to Shame; so they became as detestable as the thing they loved.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel.
God says, "I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness."
Grapes in the wilderness are rare and precious.
God says, "I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season."
Firstfruits of a fig tree are early and special.
But your fathers went to Baal-peor.
They consecrated themselves to Shame.
They became as detestable as the thing they loved.
passages.original: כַּעֲנָבִ֣ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר מָצָ֙אתִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּבִכּוּרָ֤ה בִתְאֵנָה֙ בְּרֵ֣אשִׁיתָ֔הּ רָאִ֖יתִי אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם הֵ֜מָּה בָּ֣אוּ בַֽעַל־ פְּע֗וֹר וַיִּנָּֽזְרוּ֙ לַבֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּהְי֥וּ שִׁקּוּצִ֖ים כְּאָהֳבָֽם׃

passages.text: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim once had honor and glory.
Their glory will leave them quickly.
Their glory will fly away like a bird.
They will have no children born.
There will be no pregnancies among them.
There will be no conceptions among them.
passages.original: אֶפְרַ֕יִם כָּע֖וֹף יִתְעוֹפֵ֣ף כְּבוֹדָ֑ם מִלֵּדָ֥ה וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן וּמֵהֵרָיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them of each one. Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, “Even if they raise their children, I will take their children away from them.
I will leave them without their children.
Woe will come to them when I turn away from them.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י אִם־ יְגַדְּלוּ֙ אֶת־ בְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וְשִׁכַּלְתִּ֖ים מֵֽאָדָ֑ם כִּֽי־ גַם־ א֥וֹי לָהֶ֖ם בְּשׂוּרִ֥י מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
I have seen Ephraim.
Ephraim is like Tyre.
Tyre is a city.
Tyre is planted in a pleasant meadow.
Ephraim is also planted in a pleasant place.
But Ephraim will bring out his children.
Ephraim will bring his children out to be killed.
passages.original: אֶפְרַ֛יִם כַּאֲשֶׁר־ רָאִ֥יתִי לְצ֖וֹר שְׁתוּלָ֣ה בְנָוֶ֑ה וְאֶפְרַ֕יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶל־ הֹרֵ֖ג בָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Give them, O LORD— what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!
passages.sermon:
The prophet Hosea speaks to God about the people of Israel.
He asks God to give them what they deserve.
He says, “Give them, O LORD—what will You give?”
He asks God to give them wombs that miscarry.
He asks God to give them breasts that dry up.
He asks for these things because of Israel’s sin and rebellion.
passages.original: תֵּן־ לָהֶ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מַה־ תִּתֵּ֑ן תֵּן־ לָהֶם֙ רֶ֣חֶם מַשְׁכִּ֔יל וְשָׁדַ֖יִם צֹמְקִֽים׃

passages.text: All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them. I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.
passages.sermon:
God saw all the evil of the people at Gilgal.
God hated them there.
God hated them because of their wicked actions.
God said, "I will drive them out of My house."
God said, "I will not love them anymore."
All their leaders are rebellious.
passages.original: כָּל־ רָעָתָ֤ם בַּגִּלְגָּל֙ כִּֽי־ שָׁ֣ם שְׂנֵאתִ֔ים עַ֚ל רֹ֣עַ מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם מִבֵּיתִ֖י אֲגָרְשֵׁ֑ם לֹ֤א אוֹסֵף֙ אַהֲבָתָ֔ם כָּל־ שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם סֹרְרִֽים׃

passages.text: Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered; they cannot bear fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay the darlings of their wombs.
passages.sermon:
God punished Ephraim.
Ephraim’s root is dry.
Ephraim cannot produce fruit.
If Ephraim has children, God will kill their beloved offspring.
passages.original: הֻכָּ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם שָׁרְשָׁ֥ם יָבֵ֖שׁ פְּרִ֣י בְלִי יַעֲשׂ֑וּן גַּ֚ם כִּ֣י יֵֽלֵד֔וּן וְהֵמַתִּ֖י מַחֲמַדֵּ֥י בִטְנָֽם׃ס

passages.text: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of Israel.
God will reject the people of Israel.
The people of Israel did not obey God.
Because of their disobedience, God will reject them.
The people of Israel will wander among the nations.
They will not have a home among their neighbors.
passages.original: יִמְאָסֵ֣ם אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ל֑וֹ וְיִהְי֥וּ נֹדְדִ֖ים בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃ס
